title: Ultra-Short-Term Heart Rate Variability and Measurement Limitations in Wearable Biosensors
source_organization: IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
author: Biomedical Signal Processing Committee
excerpt: Standard clinical HRV guidelines require 5-minute stationary recordings for short-term frequency and time-domain analysis. When recording windows are less than 300 seconds, RMSSD and SDNN must be explicitly designated as 'exploratory ultra-short-term measurements'. Ultra-short RMSSD remains mathematically responsive to rapid vagal shifts, but cannot be treated as clinically equivalent to standard ambulatory 24-hour Holter monitoring.

title: Electrodermal Activity Signal Dynamics and Motion Artifact Disambiguation
author: Electrodermal Standards Committee
population_studied: Wearable EDA wrist and chest sensor subjects
excerpt: Electrodermal activity recorded at 4 Hz captures sympathetic sudomotor nerve activity. True skin conductance responses (SCRs) exhibit a steep rise time (1-3 seconds) followed by an exponential decay (2-10 seconds). Mechanical electrode slips and motion artifacts manifest as instantaneous zero-latency square-wave jumps that must be filtered out using synchronized tri-axial accelerometry data.
